Job Description:
KLIC

Via KLIC (Kabels en Leidingen Informatie Centrum) verstrekt het Kadaster informatie over de ligging van kabels en leidingen. Het doel van KLIC is om graafschade te voorkomen. Bij machinale graafwerkzaamheden is het wettelijk verplicht om vooraf een KLIC-melding te doen. Of het nu gaat om een graafmelding, calamiteitenmelding of oriëntatieverzoek: met de KLIC-viewer bekijk je digitale informatie over kabels en leidingen. Voor het bekijken en afdrukken van deze informatie zijn verschillende mogelijkheden beschikbaar: via hybride apps, online browsers of desktopapplicaties.

Wat ga je doen?

In deze rol kun je écht impact maken! Je zet samen met collega’s de volgende stap in testautomatisering en test-driven development. Samen met het team onderhoud en verbeter je geautomatiseerde testcases. Vanuit jouw rol neem je de lead, behoud je het overzicht, stem je af met collega’s en zorg je voor een duidelijke verdeling van het werk. We maken hierbij gebruik van Robot Framework. Ervaring met testautomatisering is waardevol; kennis van Robot Framework is een pré. Daarnaast willen we verder groeien richting test-driven development. Testen wordt daarmee steeds meer een integraal onderdeel van het ontwikkelproces.

Jouw werkzaamheden bestaan uit:

Het ontwerpen van testspecificaties en het beheren van de testbasis, testdata en testomgeving.
Het opzetten, uitvoeren en doorontwikkelen van de KLIC-teststrategie.
Het toepassen en onderhouden van teststandaarden.
Het vaststellen en uitvoeren van functionele testen en regressietesten op de applicaties.
Het fungeren als aanspreekpunt voor testvraagstukken, het stellen van prioriteiten en het coördineren van werkzaamheden binnen het testteam.
Actieve deelname aan het scrumteam, onder andere tijdens stand-ups, refinements, retrospectives en planningssessies.
Het meedenken over en adviseren bij productie- en releaseplanningen.
Het inrichten van testomgevingen en ondersteunen bij acceptatietesten met externe partijen.
Het adviseren van de business over risico's, impact en mogelijke keuzes.

Ons team

Het KLIC team beheert en ontwikkelt een complexe Java-backend en viewers op verschillende platforms, zodat gebruikers de informatieleveringen goed kunnen bekijken. De applicaties worden gebruikt door zowel particuliere als professionele gebruikers. Je werkt in een ervaren team van professionals dat nauw samenwerkt met functioneel beheerders en productmanagement. Het testteam bestaat uit drie personen.

Het team is onderdeel van de directie BOI (Beheer en Ontwikkeling Informatietechnologie) en werkt in dynamische scrumteams van verschillende omvang. We combineren onze passie voor resultaat met een leergierige instelling, humor en oprechte interesse in elkaar. In overleg met het team werk je minimaal twee dagen per week op ons kantoor in Apeldoorn. Zo bieden we ruimte voor een gezonde werk-privébalans én krijg je de kans om te laten zien wat je in huis hebt. We werken innovatief, met moderne tooling, een vooruitstrevende architectuur en, waar mogelijk, open source software.

Heb je nog geen ervaring als Test Lead, maar zie je dat als een logische volgende stap in je ontwikkeling? Dan maken we graag kennis met je! We vinden het vooral belangrijk dat je jezelf wilt blijven ontwikkelen en de ambitie hebt om door te groeien binnen dit vakgebied.

Ervaring met het testen en automatiseren van webapplicaties, REST API's en systeemintegratietesten.

Job Description:
APM Terminals

PURPOSE:

The QA Engineer is responsible for supporting, coordinating, executing, documenting, and reporting quality assurance and testing activities related to automation products and OT deployments. This includes test preparation, test execution, defect registration and follow-up, retesting, evidence management, and readiness validation across all relevant project and product lifecycle phases.

The role helps ensure that automation solutions, OT platforms, control systems, equipment, system interfaces, operational processes, and terminal workflows are verified and validated as an integrated end-to-end solution before being introduced into live operations. Testing may include simulation and emulation, supplier and factory testing, installation verification, commissioning, integration testing, operational testing, user acceptance testing, release validation, go-live support, and post-go-live stabilization.

The QA Engineer works closely with the Quality Assurance Lead, Product Managers, Deployment Leads, terminal stakeholders, engineering teams, OT specialists, and suppliers. The role ensures that test results, defects, quality risks, dependencies, and readiness concerns are accurately documented, communicated, and followed through to resolution.

Formal business and operational acceptance remains with the appropriate accountable stakeholders. The QA Engineer provides the objective test evidence, defect information, and quality status required to support those decisions.

At APM Terminals, a global leader in port and terminal operations, we enable global trade and drive sustainable growth. What drives us forward is a mindset of always improving — observing how work happens, identifying what creates value, and removing what gets in the way. We constantly look for smarter, simpler, and safer ways of operating. If you thrive in environments where people value learning and are committed to continuously improve daily operations, join us and be a part of our journey.

What We Can Offer

At APM Terminals, we foster a dynamic learning and training culture that empowers our employees to excel. Our commitment to improvement means every team member has the opportunity to develop their skills and advance their careers by continuously refining how we work. Experience a diverse, multinational workplace where your operational insights directly influence how we work.

Work on global automation products, OT systems, and terminal deployments that support operational excellence in live terminal environments.
Collaborate with international product, engineering, deployment, supplier, and terminal operations teams across multiple locations.
Develop expertise in quality assurance, testing, commissioning, release validation, and operational readiness within a complex industrial environment.
Contribute to continuous improvement of testing processes, quality standards, tools, reporting, and knowledge sharing across the organisation.

Key Responsibilities:

Plan, prepare, coordinate, execute, document, and report testing activities across product development, deployment, commissioning, go-live, and stabilization phases.
Review business, operational, technical, interface, and safety requirements to ensure completeness, traceability, and testability.
Develop and maintain test conditions, test cases, scripts, test data requirements, acceptance criteria, and requirement-to-test traceability.
Execute and support a range of testing activities including FAT, SAT, integration, interface, operational scenario, user acceptance, regression, performance, resilience, recovery, and operational readiness testing.
Manage defects through identification, classification, tracking, retesting, closure, trend analysis, root cause investigation, and stakeholder escalation where required.
Review supplier test documentation, release evidence, defect resolution activities, and quality records to ensure compliance with agreed requirements.
Support readiness reviews, quality reporting, go-live assessments, operational handovers, and continuous improvement initiatives across automation and OT deployments.

What We Are Looking For:

Continuous improvement mindset: we are looking for someone who brings a thoughtful improvement mindset—curious about how work gets done and motivated to make meaningful, sustainable improvements over time.
Leadership expectation: We are looking for people who consistently put customers first, lead by example with respect for people, deliver results with integrity, and drive continuous improvement by solving problems at the root, developing people, and raising standards every day.
Bachelor’s degree in Automation Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Mechatronics, Systems Engineering, Quality Management, or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant professional experience.
Professional experience in quality assurance, system testing, product validation, commissioning, industrial automation, operational technology (OT), or other complex industrial technology environments.
Strong understanding of automation equipment, control systems, system integrations, software and firmware releases, commissioning activities, and live operational environments.
Experience creating and executing structured test cases, managing test evidence, maintaining traceability, and supporting defect management throughout the testing lifecycle.
Familiarity with test and defect management tools such as Jira, Xray, or equivalent platforms, combined with strong analytical, documentation, and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to communicate quality risks, defects, readiness status, and testing outcomes clearly while working effectively across global, cross-functional, and multicultural teams.
English proficiency is required; additional language skills relevant to terminal locations are advantageous.

The QA Engineer plays a critical role in ensuring the quality, reliability, performance, and deployment readiness of automation products and OT systems operating within complex terminal environments. Working closely with Product Managers, Deployment Leads, engineering teams, operational stakeholders, and external suppliers, you will provide the structured testing, defect management, quality evidence, and readiness insights required to support safe and successful deployments. The role includes participation in office, supplier, project, laboratory, emulation, and live terminal environments and may require international travel and occasional work outside standard office hours during planned testing or deployment windows.

Replit is the agentic software creation platform that enables anyone to build applications using natural language. With millions of users worldwide, Replit is democratizing software development by removing traditional barriers to application creation.

About the role:

Join our Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) team and help ensure the reliability, scalability, and performance of Replit's infrastructure that serves millions of developers worldwide. As a Staff Site Reliability Engineer, you will bridge the gap between development and operations, implementing automation and establishing best practices that enable our platform to scale efficiently while maintaining high availability.

We are seeking Staff SREs who are passionate about building and maintaining resilient systems at scale. Your mission will be to proactively find and analyze reliability problems across our stack, then design and implement software and systems to create step-function improvements. You will design robust observability solutions, lead incident response, automate operational tasks, and continuously improve our infrastructure's reliability, all while mentoring and educating the broader engineering team to make reliability a core value at Replit.

You Will:

Architect and Implement Observability: Design, build, and lead the implementation of comprehensive monitoring, logging, and tracing solutions. Create dashboards and metrics that provide real-time visibility into system health and performance, enabling proactive issue detection. 
Define and Drive Reliability Standards: Work with product and engineering teams to define, implement, and track Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and Service Level Indicators (SLIs). Build systems to monitor and report on these metrics, holding teams accountable and ensuring we maintain high reliability standards while balancing innovation speed. 
Lead Incident Management and Response: Act as a senior leader during high-impact incidents, guiding the team to rapid resolution. Conduct thorough, blameless post-mortems and drive the implementation of preventative measures. Develop and refine runbooks and build automation to reduce Mean Time To Recovery (MTTR). 
Drive Automation and Infrastructure as Code: Architect, build, and improve automation to eliminate toil and operational work. Design and maintain CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure automation using tools like Terraform or Pulumi. Create self-healing systems that can automatically respond to common failure scenarios. 
Optimize Performance on Kubernetes: Collaborate with core infrastructure and product teams to performance-tune and optimize our large-scale cloud deployments, with a deep focus on Kubernetes, Docker, and GCP. Identify and resolve performance bottlenecks, implement capacity planning strategies, and reduce latency across global regions. 
Debug and Harden Distributed Systems: Dive deep into debugging extremely difficult technical problems across the stack. Use your findings to design and implement long-term fixes that make our systems and products more robust, operable, and easier to diagnose. 
Provide Staff-Level Guidance: Review feature and system designs from across the company, acting as a key owner for the reliability, scalability, security, and operational integrity of those designs. 
Educate and Mentor: Educate, mentor, and hold accountable the broader engineering team to improve the reliability of our systems, making reliability a core value of the Replit engineering culture. 
Build and Integrate: Write high-quality, well-tested code in Python or Go to meet the needs of your customers, whether it's building new internal tools or integrating with third-party vendors. 

Required Skills and Experience:

8-10 years of experience in Site Reliability Engineering or similar roles (e.g., DevOps, Systems Engineering, Infrastructure Engineering). 
Strong programming skills in languages like Python or Go. You write high-quality, well-tested code. 
Deep understanding of distributed systems. You’ve designed, built, scaled, and maintained production services and know how to compose a service-oriented architecture. 
Deep experience with container orchestration platforms, specifically Kubernetes, and cloud-native technologies. 
Proven track record of designing, implementing, and maintaining sophisticated monitoring and observability solutions (e.g., metrics, logging, tracing). 
Strong incident management skills with extensive experience leading incident response for complex systems and demonstrated critical thinking under pressure. 
Experience with infrastructure as code (e.g., Terraform, Pulumi) and configuration management tools. 
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with an ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly and simply and a bias toward open, transparent cultural practices. 
Strong interpersonal skills, with experience working with and mentoring engineers from junior to principal levels. 
A willingness to dive into understanding, debugging, and improving any layer of the stack. 
You're passionate about making software creation accessible and empowering the next generation of builders. 

Bonus Points:

Deep experience with Google Cloud Platform (GCP) services and tools. 
Expert-level knowledge of modern observability platforms (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, OpenTelemetry). 
Experience designing and building reliable systems capable of handling high throughput and low latency. 
Significant experience with Go and Terraform.
